_note: The memory ablation, which is the one paired comparison runnable before any method exists: the method library is empty until runs with repair rounds have been distilled, so A-vs-B on a flat method library has no B yet. What this measures instead is whether the capsule helps at all — the same briefs with the project's memory records active and with them parked. EvoMemBench's finding is the hypothesis worth testing: memory helps hard tasks and can hurt easy ones, so the two arms are expected to differ by brief rather than uniformly.
_recordsPending: `records` are empty here because the control plane has no route that creates a memory record — GET /api/memory/records lists, PATCH /api/memory/records/<id> updates, and nothing posts. Records exist only where the extractor put them. So the seeding step is a small set of real runs on this project that state preferences outright, after which both arms name the same record ids: baseline parks them (status pending), candidate activates them (status active). Filling these in from an invented id would produce a run that patches nothing and two arms that are the same arm.
